questions.q: What are the two complementary ways to find assets in the Purview catalog?
options: Search and browse
Export and import
Scan and classify
Request and approve
questions.explain: Search lets you type keywords or phrases; browse lets you explore by collection, source type, or domain without typing a query.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid way to narrow a Purview search query, per the lesson?
options: Combining terms with AND, OR, NOT, or an exact phrase in double quotes
Only ever typing a single whole word with no punctuation
Disabling the filter pane entirely
Searching exclusively by file size
questions.explain: Purview search syntax supports operators like AND, OR, NOT, and exact-phrase quotes to combine keywords precisely.

questions.q: What makes "governed assets search" different from searching all assets?
options: It returns only assets carrying governance metadata, such as a glossary term, data product membership, or data quality score
It only searches file names, never descriptions
It is only available to tenant administrators
It searches exclusively Power BI content
questions.explain: Governed assets search is a focused search surfacing only curated, governed assets — each marked "Governed" in the results.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what does the Purview relevance engine favor when ranking search results?
options: An asset curated by a data steward with a good description tends to outrank an unannotated folder that merely matches a keyword
Results are always sorted alphabetically with no ranking logic
Only the most recently created asset is ever shown first
Classification labels are ignored entirely in ranking
questions.explain: The relevance engine weighs many factors, and a well-curated asset tends to rank above an unannotated one that just happens to match a keyword.

questions.q: What's the key lesson from an asset detail page that has no description, classifications, or glossary terms?
options: Being searchable and being useful are not the same thing — an uncurated asset is findable but tells a searcher almost nothing
Such an asset should be deleted from Data Map immediately
It means the asset was never scanned
It means Purview search is broken
questions.explain: Data Map makes an asset findable the moment it's scanned, but curation (covered in Lesson 21) is what makes a found asset actually useful to a searcher.
